userStories.title: Start the userspace Tailscale daemon where the verb runs
userStories.description: As a node owner, I want `enable` to install Tailscale and start one userspace daemon on this machine. The plain `tailscale` CLI then works with no `--socket` flag.
acceptanceCriteria: The verb acts on the machine where it runs. The verb never uses `docker exec` and never targets another container.
If `tailscale` is not on `PATH`, `enable` runs the `tailscale` catalog install argv from `.agro/cli/src/lib/tools/catalog.ts` on this machine.

If `/run/systemd/system` exists, `enable` writes `/etc/systemd/system/agro-tailscaled.service` through `sudo -n`, runs `sudo -n systemctl daemon-reload`, and runs `sudo -n systemctl enable --now agro-tailscaled.service`.

The unit text equals the console unit in `mifunedev/agro-console` `packages/shared/src/tailscaled-assets.ts`: - `--tun=userspace-networking --statedir=<home>/.tailscale` - `RuntimeDirectory=tailscale` - `RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755` - `Conflicts=tailscaled.service` - `User=` and `Group=` set to the invoking user
If `/run/systemd/system` does not exist, `enable` starts `tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking --statedir=$HOME/.tailscale` in the detached tmux session `agent-tailscaled`.
If the unit file already has the same text, `enable` does not write the file again. If the daemon already answers `tailscale status`, `enable` does not start a second daemon.
Tests with an injected runner cover the systemd path, the tmux path, the missing-binary install, and the second run with no change.

userStories.title: Connect, publish, pair, disable, and report status
userStories.description: As a node owner, I want `enable`, `pair`, `disable`, and `status` to call the upstream `tailscale` and `t3` commands. I then pair my phone with one command and manage access later.
acceptanceCriteria: After US-002, `enable` runs these commands in order and stops at the first nonzero exit status: 1. `tailscale up`, which prints the login URL; 2. `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:3773`; 3. the pair command.
The pair command is `t3 pair --tailscale` when `t3` is on `PATH`. Otherwise the pair command is `npx --yes t3@latest pair --tailscale`.
`pair` runs the pair command only.
`disable` runs `tailscale serve --https=443 off`.
`status` runs `tailscale status` and then `tailscale serve status`.
Each action passes stdin, stdout, and stderr of the upstream command through. The verb exits with the exit status of the first command that fails, or 0.
The verb has no `update` action, and the verb parses no upstream output.
Tests with an injected runner assert the argv order, the stop at the first failure, the exit status passthrough, and the pair-command choice.
userStories.notes: 54967f54 cherry-picked. enable order up -> serve -> pair, stop at first failure; pair command choice t3 vs npx t3@latest; pair/disable/status argv; status runs both; stdio inherit; exit passthrough: executed t3-mobile.test.ts (red 17 fail, green); t3-mobile + cli-first-help 64 passed exit 0 on task branch. No update action: executed help output lists 4 actions. typecheck exit 0; build exit 0; dist help exit 0. Interactive tailscale up login URL: reasoned (stdio inherit), US-006 runs it. Note: a nonzero step adds one stderr line naming the command.
